requirements.title: Start an attempt: workspace state, upstream fetch and upstream base
requirements.rationale: Every rebuild starts from the upstream as it is now, and a workspace that cannot be rebuilt must end the job in the way that says whether trying again can help.

criteria.condition: a worker starts an attempt of a rebuild job whose carry-patch workspace is in status ready
criteria.action: fetch upstream with the upstream credentials into refs/remotes/upstream/* without tags, resolve the upstream base as the head of the upstream's default branch, store it on the job as upstream_head_sha and empty the job's patch_results
criteria.contract: the job record has upstream_head_sha equal to the 40-character head of the upstream's default branch after the fetch and patch_results []; refs/remotes/upstream/<branch> equals each upstream branch; no ref under refs/tags/ is created; the fetch used UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT when set, else UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD, else the origin credential of the workspace

setup: the rebuild fixture, built in this file and reused by every test of the package: an upstream bare repository, an origin bare repository and the hub's bare repository made with git in t.TempDir(); a carry-patch workspace record in status ready with integration_branch deploy in a real store in t.TempDir(); patches registered in the store with their branches in the hub repository; a queued rebuild job claimed for one attempt; a fixed clock; a recording event emitter; the landing identity Parley <parley@localhost>; hooks the test can set to run code before a given patch and before the publish
for the credential table: a recording fetcher in place of the git fetch
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_FetchesUpstreamAndRecordsBase: add commit U2 and tag v9 to upstream after the workspace was set up; run one attempt; assert job.upstream_head_sha == U2; assert ref refs/remotes/upstream/main == U2; assert no ref refs/tags/v9 in the hub repository; assert job.patch_results == [] for a job record that carried results of an earlier attempt. Then a table over the secrets {UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT set -> resolver returns the token, only UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME and UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD -> that pair, none -> the origin credential}: assert the credential the recording fetcher received

criteria.condition: the upstream's default branch is unknown after the fetch and upstream has a branch named like the workspace's default_branch
criteria.action: use the head of that upstream branch as the upstream base
criteria.contract: the job's upstream_head_sha equals the head of refs/remotes/upstream/<default_branch of the workspace>

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_BaseFallsBackToWorkspaceDefaultBranch: upstream has branches trunk and release and no resolvable default branch (its HEAD names a branch that does not exist); the workspace's default_branch is release; run one attempt; assert job.upstream_head_sha == head of upstream release

criteria.condition: the upstream fetch fails, or neither the upstream's default branch nor an upstream branch named like the workspace's default_branch resolves
criteria.action: end the attempt as a retryable failure without reading a patch branch, changing a patch or moving the integration branch
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is a retryable failure with reason upstream_fetch_failed for a failed fetch and upstream_unknown for a base that does not resolve; patch_results is []; the integration branch and every patch record are unchanged

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_UpstreamFailuresAreRetryable, a table over {the upstream repository directory removed -> upstream_fetch_failed, upstream reachable with no default branch and no branch named like default_branch -> upstream_unknown}: out = run one attempt; assert out.kind == retryable and out.reason == want; assert job.patch_results == []; assert the head of deploy and the patch rows equal their values before the attempt

criteria.condition: the workspace of the job is in status archived or failed when an attempt starts
criteria.action: end the attempt as a permanent failure without fetching upstream
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is a permanent failure with reason workspace_archived for archived and workspace_not_ready for failed, so the job is dead-lettered without retry; the fetch is not started

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
a recording fetcher in place of the git fetch
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_WorkspaceStateAtStart, a table over the workspace status {archived -> permanent workspace_archived, failed -> permanent workspace_not_ready, pending -> retryable workspace_busy, cloning -> retryable workspace_busy}: out = run one attempt; assert out.kind and out.reason; assert fetcher.calls == 0

criteria.condition: the workspace of the job is in status pending or cloning when an attempt starts
criteria.action: end the attempt as a retryable failure without fetching upstream
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is a retryable failure with reason workspace_busy; the fetch is not started

criteria.condition: the workspace stops being ready while an attempt runs, because it was archived, recloned or deleted
criteria.action: end the attempt at its next step, before the next patch or inside the publish, without moving the integration branch
criteria.contract: archived or failed: permanent failure with reason workspace_archived or workspace_not_ready; pending or cloning: retryable failure with reason workspace_busy; deleted: the attempt ends, writes no job or patch record and emits no event; in every case the integration branch is at the head it had before the attempt

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_WorkspaceLeavesReadyDuringRun, a table over {archive before patch 2 -> permanent workspace_archived, status cloning before the publish -> retryable workspace_busy, workspace and its jobs deleted before patch 2 -> ended with nothing written}: set the hook; out = run one attempt; assert out; assert head of deploy == its head before the attempt (where the repository still exists); for the deleted row assert the emitter recorded no event after the deletion and no job row exists

requirements.title: Fix the patch list of a run and report progress
requirements.rationale: A run that reads branch tips once cannot mix two states of a patch, and a job that shows each patch as it finishes lets a waiting caller see where a long rebuild stands.

criteria.condition: the upstream base of an attempt is resolved
criteria.action: list the non-deleted patches of the workspace in position order and record the present tip of each patch branch as that patch's source_sha, null when the branch does not exist
criteria.contract: patch_results, once the run has processed every patch, holds one entry per non-deleted patch in position order, each with the patch_id, branch_name and position the patch had at the listing and the source_sha read at the listing; deleted patches have no entry

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_ListsPatchesInPositionOrder: patches p1, p2 and p3, all active, registered at positions 1, 2 and 3 in an order other than their creation order, and a soft-deleted p4; run one attempt; assert [r.patch_id for r in job.patch_results] == [p1, p2, p3]; assert each r.position and r.branch_name; assert each r.source_sha == the tip its branch had before the attempt

criteria.condition: an attempt is running
criteria.action: use only the source_sha recorded at the listing for every patch, and accept updates of patch branches by other callers without waiting for the attempt
criteria.contract: a compare-and-swap of a patch branch made during the run succeeds at once; the published integration head contains the commits of the recorded source_sha of that patch and not the commit added during the run

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches p1 and p2
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_PushDuringRunDoesNotChangeTheResult: hook before patch 1: move the branch of p2 from its tip T to a new commit X with the compare-and-swap of internal/gitrepo and assert it returns no error; run one attempt to completion; assert patch_results[1].source_sha == T; assert the commit message of X is absent from git log of deploy and the change of T is present in the tree of deploy

criteria.condition: the run reaches a patch that is disabled, that is merged_upstream, or whose branch does not exist
criteria.action: record the patch as skipped with the reason disabled, merged_upstream or branch_not_found and leave the head under construction as it is
criteria.contract: the patch result has status skipped, skipped_reason one of disabled, merged_upstream, branch_not_found, new_head_sha null, conflict_files [] and conflict null; the published head contains no commit of that patch

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_SkipsPatchesThatDoNotApplyToTheRun, a table over {status disabled -> disabled, status merged_upstream -> merged_upstream, status active with its branch deleted -> branch_not_found (source_sha null)}: run one attempt with strategy rebase; r = the patch's result; assert r.status == 'skipped' and r.skipped_reason == want and r.new_head_sha == null and r.conflict_files == [] and r.conflict == null; assert head of deploy == the upstream base when it is the only patch

criteria.condition: the run reaches a patch whose status is conflict
criteria.action: apply the patch as it applies an active patch
criteria.contract: a patch in status conflict whose branch now applies has the result status success with a new_head_sha

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_TriesConflictPatchesAgain: one patch in status conflict with conflict_files ['f.txt'] whose branch applies to the upstream base; run one attempt; assert patch_results[0].status == 'success' and patch_results[0].new_head_sha == head of deploy

criteria.condition: the run finishes a patch as success, conflict or skipped
criteria.action: store the results so far on the job before starting the next patch
criteria.contract: a read of the running job's record between two patches returns status running and patch_results with exactly the patches finished so far, in position order; patches_applied, patches_skipped, patches_conflicted and patches_removed are 0 while the job is not completed

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_StoresProgressAfterEveryPatch: three active patches; hook before patch 2 and before patch 3 reads the job record from the store; assert len(patch_results) == 1 then 2, each a prefix of the final list; assert the four counts are 0 at both reads and job.status == 'running'

criteria.action: for any patch result, set new_head_sha only when status is success, skipped_reason only when status is skipped, and conflict_files and conflict only when status is conflict, with every member present in the JSON
criteria.contract: patch result members: patch_id, branch_name, position, status (success | conflict | skipped), skipped_reason (string or null), source_sha (40 hex or null), new_head_sha (40 hex or null), conflict_files (string list, [] unless conflict), conflict (conflict report or null)

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/result_test.go, TestPatchResult_JSONShapeByStatus, a table over one result of each status {success, conflict, skipped with each of the four reasons}: j = json.Marshal(result); assert every one of the nine members is a key of j; assert the members that the status does not set are null, or [] for conflict_files

requirements.title: Build the new head from the upstream base and the patches
requirements.rationale: The integration branch is defined as the upstream base plus every applicable patch in order; the two strategies are the two ways a team wants that history to look.

criteria.condition: the run applies a patch with strategy rebase
criteria.action: replay every commit that is reachable from the patch's source_sha and not from the upstream base, oldest first, onto the head under construction, keeping each commit's author, author date and message and setting the committer to the hub's landing identity, and record the patch as success
criteria.contract: the patch result has status success and new_head_sha equal to the head under construction after the patch; the commits between the previous head under construction and new_head_sha are as many as the replayed commits, in the same order, each with the original author name, author email, author date and message and with committer [land].committer_name <[land].committer_email>; the first patch is applied onto the upstream base and each later patch onto the new_head_sha of the last applied patch

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_RebaseReplaysCommitsInOrder: p1 has commits a1, a2 by author Ada <ada@example.com>; p2 has commit b1 by Bo <bo@example.com>; upstream has moved by one commit since the branches were cut; run one attempt with strategy rebase; log = git log --reverse base..deploy; assert the messages are [a1, a2, b1]; assert each author and author date equals the original; assert every committer is 'Parley <parley@localhost>'; assert patch_results[0].new_head_sha == the commit carrying a2 and patch_results[1].new_head_sha == head of deploy; assert the parent of the commit carrying a1 == the upstream base

criteria.condition: a patch applied with strategy rebase has a merge commit, or a commit whose change is already present in the head under construction from upstream or from an earlier patch
criteria.action: leave the merge commit out and drop the commit whose change is already present, replaying the other commits
criteria.contract: the commits added for the patch are its non-merge commits whose change is not already present; no commit added by the run has two parents and none has an empty diff

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_RebaseLeavesOutMergesAndDropsPresentCommits, a table over {the patch branch holds c1, a merge of upstream into the branch, then c2 -> added [c1, c2]; the patch holds c1 and c2 where upstream has since applied the same change as c1 -> added [c2]; patch p2 was cut from the branch of p1 and so holds p1's commit a1 and its own b1 -> added for p2 is [b1]}: run one attempt with strategy rebase; assert the messages of the commits added for the patch; assert every added commit has one parent and a non-empty diff

criteria.condition: a patch has no commit left to replay with strategy rebase, or its source_sha is already reachable from the head under construction with strategy merge
criteria.action: record the patch as skipped with the reason nothing_to_apply and leave the head under construction as it is
criteria.contract: the patch result has status skipped, skipped_reason nothing_to_apply and new_head_sha null; the head under construction after the patch equals the head before it

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_NothingToApply, a table over {rebase: the patch branch points at the upstream base; rebase: the only commit of the patch is already present in upstream as another commit; merge: the patch branch points at an ancestor of the upstream base}: run one attempt; assert the result is skipped with nothing_to_apply and new_head_sha null; assert head of deploy == the upstream base

criteria.condition: the run applies a patch with strategy merge
criteria.action: merge the patch's source_sha into the head under construction with a merge commit, even when a fast-forward is possible, and record the patch as success
criteria.contract: new_head_sha is a commit with two parents, the first the head under construction before the patch and the second the patch's source_sha, with the message "Merge branch '<branch_name>'" and with author and committer [land].committer_name <[land].committer_email>

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch on branch feature/x
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_MergeAlwaysMakesAMergeCommit, a table over {the patch branch is ahead of the upstream base and could fast-forward; upstream has moved so a real merge is needed}: run one attempt with strategy merge; m = patch_results[0].new_head_sha; assert parents(m) == [head under construction before, source_sha]; assert subject(m) == "Merge branch 'feature/x'"; assert author(m) == committer(m) == 'Parley <parley@localhost>'; assert head of deploy == m

criteria.action: for any commit a rebuild creates, take the committer name and email from the server configuration [land].committer_name and [land].committer_email and never from the environment of the parleyd process or the configuration of the repository
criteria.contract: with GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL set in the process environment and user.name set in the repository's configuration, every commit of a rebuild has the configured landing identity as committer, and a replayed commit keeps its original author

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_CommitterComesFromConfiguration: t.Setenv the four GIT_* identity variables to Mallory; git config user.name Mallory in the hub repository; landing identity configured as Hub Bot <bot@hub.example>; run one attempt per strategy {rebase, merge}; assert every commit in base..deploy has committer 'Hub Bot <bot@hub.example>'; with rebase assert the author is the original author; assert 'Mallory' appears in no commit

criteria.condition: an attempt is running and has not reached the publish
criteria.action: build the head under construction in a scratch working tree that no ref points to, changing no ref of the repository other than those under refs/remotes/upstream/
criteria.contract: at every moment before the publish, the output of git for-each-ref restricted to refs/heads/, refs/tags/ and refs/parley/ equals its output before the attempt, and the ref advertisement of the repository lists no commit the run created

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go, TestRebuild_BuildsOutOfSight: before = git for-each-ref refs/heads refs/tags refs/parley; hooks before patch 2 and before the publish: assert git for-each-ref of the same prefixes == before, and assert git ls-remote of the hub repository lists none of the new_head_sha values stored so far; run one attempt with strategy rebase

requirements.title: Report a conflicting patch and follow the fail mode
requirements.rationale: A team must learn which patch stopped applying, on which files and against what, in the same form a landing conflict has, and must be able to choose between an unchanged branch and a branch without the broken patch.

criteria.condition: a commit of a patch, or with strategy merge the patch tip, does not apply and at least one path is left in conflict after remembered resolutions were replayed
criteria.action: undo the patch so that the head under construction is what it was before the patch, set the patch's status to conflict and its conflict_files to the paths left in conflict ordered by path, record the patch result as conflict, and emit parley.patch.update when the status changed
criteria.contract: the patch record has status conflict and conflict_files equal to the conflicted paths in ascending order; the patch result has status conflict, the same conflict_files, new_head_sha null and a conflict report; a patch that was active produces one event parley.patch.update with resource_type patch, resource_id the patch id, actor system and metadata {branch_name, changed: ["status"], from: "active", to: "conflict", reason: "rebuild_conflict"}; a patch that was already conflict produces no parley.patch.update; none of the commits of the undone patch is reachable from the head the run goes on with

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch p1 of two commits
a stub conflict-file describer returning one content entry per conflicted path
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go, TestRebuild_ConflictUndoesThePatchAndMarksIt: p1 changes line 3 of b.txt and a.txt where upstream changed the same lines, in its second commit; its first commit applies; run one attempt with fail_mode continue and strategy rebase; assert patch p1 in the store: status conflict, conflict_files ['a.txt', 'b.txt']; assert result: status conflict, conflict_files the same, new_head_sha null, conflict != null; assert one parley.patch.update with the metadata above; assert head of deploy == the upstream base (the first commit of p1 is not in it). Run a second attempt of a new job: assert no further parley.patch.update for p1

criteria.condition: a patch is recorded as conflict
criteria.action: produce a conflict report with the patch id, the head under construction before the patch as target_sha, the patch's source_sha as head_sha, the merge base of source_sha and target_sha as base_sha, the first commit that did not apply as commit_sha (with strategy merge the source_sha), one files entry per path still in conflict, an empty landed_changes and a null change
criteria.contract: conflict report: {patch_id: string, target_sha: 40 hex, head_sha: 40 hex, base_sha: 40 hex, commit_sha: 40 hex, files: [{path, kind, base, ours, theirs, landed_by: []}] ordered by path, landed_changes: [], change: null}; ours is the file in target_sha and theirs the file in commit_sha; target_sha is the upstream base for the first applied patch and the new_head_sha of the last applied patch otherwise

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
a recording conflict-file describer that returns, for each path it is given, a content entry whose ours and theirs name the blobs of that path in the two commits it is given
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go, TestRebuild_ConflictReportMembers, a table over {rebase, the conflicting patch first: target_sha == upstream base, commit_sha == the second commit of the patch; rebase, the conflicting patch after an applied patch p0: target_sha == patch_results[0].new_head_sha; merge: commit_sha == source_sha}: run one attempt with fail_mode continue; rep = the conflict of the patch result; assert rep.patch_id, rep.target_sha, rep.head_sha == source_sha, rep.base_sha == git merge-base source_sha target_sha, rep.commit_sha; assert the describer was called once with (target_sha, commit_sha, ['a.txt']); assert rep.files == the entries it returned, each with landed_by []; assert rep.landed_changes == [] and rep.change == null and that the JSON has all eight members

criteria.condition: a patch is recorded as conflict and the job's fail_mode is fail_fast
criteria.action: stop the run without processing a later patch and without moving the integration branch, and end the attempt as a permanent failure that carries the conflict report
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is a permanent failure with reason conflict that carries the patch's conflict report and a text naming the patch's branch, which dead-letters the job without retry; patch_results ends with the conflicting patch; the four counts are 0; integration_head_sha is null; the integration branch is at the head it had before the attempt; no later patch is changed

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with three active patches p1 (applies), p2 on branch feature/b (conflicts) and p3 (applies), fail_mode fail_fast
a stub conflict-file describer returning one content entry per conflicted path
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go, TestRebuild_FailFastStopsAndPublishesNothing: before = head of deploy; out = run one attempt; assert out.kind == permanent and out.reason == 'conflict'; assert out.conflict == patch_results[1].conflict and 'feature/b' in out.text; assert len(job.patch_results) == 2; assert the four counts == 0 and job.integration_head_sha == null; assert head of deploy == before; assert patch p3 is unchanged in the store

criteria.condition: a patch is recorded as conflict and the job's fail_mode is continue
criteria.action: go on with the next patch from the head under construction before the conflicting patch and publish the integration branch without the conflicting patch
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is completed; patch_results has the conflicting patch as conflict and the patches after it with their own results; the patch after the conflicting one is applied onto the new_head_sha of the last applied patch before it; the published head contains the commits of the applied patches and none of the conflicting patch

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with three active patches p1 (applies), p2 (conflicts) and p3 (applies)
a stub conflict-file describer returning one content entry per conflicted path
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go, TestRebuild_ContinuePublishesWithoutTheConflictingPatch: same three patches, fail_mode continue; out = run one attempt; assert out.kind == completed; assert [r.status for r in job.patch_results] == ['success', 'conflict', 'success']; assert the parent of the first commit of p3 on deploy == patch_results[0].new_head_sha; assert the parent chain of deploy holds the commits of p1 and p3 and no commit of p2; assert patch p2 has status conflict in the store

criteria.condition: a git operation of the run fails for a reason other than a conflict, or runs longer than 10 minutes, or the attempt's context is cancelled because the hub shuts down
criteria.action: end the attempt as a retryable failure without recording a skip, a conflict or a success for the patch in work, without changing a patch record and without moving the integration branch
criteria.contract: the attempt's outcome is a retryable failure with reason git_error for a failed git operation, timeout for one over the limit (its git process and child processes are killed) and shutdown for a cancelled context; patch_results holds no entry for the patch in work; every patch record and the integration branch are as before the attempt

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches
the per-operation time limit injectable for the test; its production value is 10 minutes
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go, TestRebuild_NonConflictFailuresAreRetryable, a table over {a commit object of patch 2 removed from the object store before patch 2 -> git_error; the per-operation limit set to 50 ms and the git runner made to sleep on the replay of patch 2 -> timeout; the context cancelled before patch 2 -> shutdown}: out = run one attempt; assert out.kind == retryable and out.reason == want; assert len(job.patch_results) == 1; assert patch 2 keeps status active and conflict_files []; assert head of deploy is unchanged; for timeout assert no git child process of the attempt is alive after it returns

requirements.title: Replay and learn remembered resolutions
requirements.rationale: A carried patch meets the same conflict every time upstream moves near it; a resolution the team gave once should not have to be given again.

criteria.condition: a commit of a patch does not apply and a resolution is recorded in the workspace for the conflict of every conflicted path
criteria.action: replay the recorded resolutions, count the commit as applied with the resolved content and go on with the run
criteria.contract: the patch result is success; the file at each resolved path in new_head_sha has the recorded resolved content and no conflict marker; the patch's status is not set to conflict

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch that conflicts with upstream in a.txt
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_rerere_test.go, TestRebuild_ReplaysARecordedResolution: seed the hub repository's rerere store with the resolution R for the conflict between upstream's line and the patch's line in a.txt (by resolving that conflict once in a scratch working tree with rerere on); run one attempt; assert patch_results[0].status == 'success'; assert a.txt in deploy == R and contains no '<<<<<<<'; assert the patch is active

criteria.condition: recorded resolutions resolve some of the conflicted paths of a commit and leave at least one path in conflict
criteria.action: record the patch as conflict and list only the paths still in conflict in conflict_files and in the conflict report
criteria.contract: conflict_files of the patch and of its result, and the paths of the conflict report's files, are exactly the paths without a recorded resolution

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go
a stub conflict-file describer returning one content entry per conflicted path
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_rerere_test.go, TestRebuild_ReportsOnlyPathsLeftInConflict: the patch conflicts in a.txt and b.txt; a resolution is seeded for a.txt only; run one attempt with fail_mode continue; assert the patch's conflict_files == ['b.txt']; assert [f.path for f in result.conflict.files] == ['b.txt']

criteria.condition: git records a conflict during a run
criteria.action: keep one entry for the workspace with the id git gave the conflict, the path of the file, resolved false and recorded_at the present time, and keep the workspace's resolutions in that workspace's repository only
criteria.contract: after a run that left a.txt in conflict, the workspace's remembered-resolution entries contain {id: the rerere id, path: "a.txt", resolved: false, recorded_at: the clock's time}; a second run that meets the same conflict adds no second entry; another workspace with the same conflict has no entry from this workspace and replays none of its resolutions

setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with one active patch that conflicts with upstream in a.txt
for the second test a second workspace with its own repositories and the same commits
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_rerere_test.go, TestRebuild_RecordsUnresolvedConflicts: run one attempt with fail_mode continue; e = entries of the workspace; assert len(e) == 1 and e[0].path == 'a.txt' and e[0].resolved == false and e[0].recorded_at == clock.now and e[0].id == the directory name under the repository's rr-cache; run a second job's attempt; assert len(entries) == 1. TestRebuild_ResolutionsArePerWorkspace: seed a resolution in workspace A; run the same conflict in workspace B; assert B's patch result is conflict and B's entries hold only B's own unresolved entry

criteria.condition: paths are left in conflict after recorded resolutions were replayed and the patch has merge commits with two parents among the commits reachable from its source_sha and not from the upstream base
criteria.action: redo each of those merges, the newest 50 at most, in the scratch working tree; where a redone merge conflicts, record the merge commit's content of the conflicted files as the resolution of that conflict; then try the commit that did not apply once more
criteria.contract: when the patch branch holds a merge of the upstream base that resolved the conflict, the patch result is success and the file in new_head_sha has the content the merge commit gave it; the entry of that conflict has resolved true and recorded_at the time of the learning; a later run on a workspace whose patch branch no longer holds the merge commit, meeting the same conflict, also ends success; a patch whose merge commits do not resolve the conflict is recorded as conflict
